MET-ENFORCE-029's adopted architecture/compiled-filter-programs-v2/status.json has reviewRounds entries ({round, record, recordSha256, subject, verdict, findings}) and a carriedNotes map. That map is where v2's R1-1 (git modes and the complete file set) and R1-7 reached the mechanics layer. v2's README cites no review-note id. At adoption: copy both review records into the directory, list them in reviewRounds, and add carriedNotes for P3R1-2 (git modes and the complete file set of compiled-filter-programs-v3/), P3R1-3 (the packet's layer restates x86_64 49/50/288 and aarch64 200/201/242) and P3R1-4 (edge v6, status.json, the quotes and the status lines). The README's P3R1-5 reference then resolves to review-round1.json.

P3R1-5, vectors: README.md:142-146 was checked against v5's vectors.json. OBSERVER has 22 listener rows per architecture (18 accept4, 2 bind, 2 listen; 44 in all). bind uses two distinct arg sets, all zero and (7, 0x7fff0000, 0x10); listen uses all zero and (7, 0x80); all four rows are ALLOW. The accept4 rows include, as KILL_PROCESS, 0x800 alone, 0x40000, bit 0 and bit 31, and, as ALLOW, 0, 0x80000 and 0x80800 under high word 0xffffffff. Every accept4 claim in the paragraph is therefore vector-backed. No role has a plain-accept vector (0 rows with nr 43 on x86_64 or 202 on aarch64). FIXED.

OBSERVER's duties and its NATIVE_STATIC base name no plain accept, and v5's defaultAction is KILL_PROCESS. The reviewer's own small interpreter gives these results on both architectures: plain accept under 3 argument sets reaches the final RET KILL_PROCESS (pc 252 on x86_64, 241 on aarch64); bind and listen are ALLOW under zero, all-ones and mixed arguments; 44 of 44 listener vectors give their recorded action.
